theorems.name: Bond Portfolio First-Order Immunization
theorems.description: If the duration-times-value of the asset portfolio matches that of the liability, the net portfolio's first-order rate sensitivity is zero: ∂(A - L)/∂r = 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.Immunization

open MathFin

theorem bond_immunization_first_order_thm
    {ι κ : Type*}
    (sA : Finset ι) (wA TA : ι → ℝ)
    (sL : Finset κ) (wL TL : κ → ℝ)
    (t r : ℝ)
    (h_match : MathFin.bondPortfolioDur sA wA TA t r =
               MathFin.bondPortfolioDur sL wL TL t r) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r' =>
        MathFin.bondPortfolioValue sA wA TA t r' -
        MathFin.bondPortfolioValue sL wL TL t r')
      0 r :=
  MathFin.bondPortfolio_immunization_first_order sA wA TA sL wL TL t r h_match

theorems.name: Bond Portfolio Second-Order Immunization
theorems.description: Matching the convexity-times-value Σᵢ wᵢ(Tᵢ − t)²·e^{−r(Tᵢ − t)} of the asset and liability bond portfolios gives ∂²(A − L)/∂r² = 0 at the current rate r: the surplus has zero second rate-derivative. The statement assumes only the convexity-times-value match; matching duration-times-value is the separate first-order condition. Redington's second-order condition is the strict inequality ∂²A/∂r² > ∂²L/∂r², with values and first derivatives matched, which makes the surplus a local minimum. This entry is the equality boundary, where the second-order term vanishes, and claims no minimum.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.ConvexityImmunization

open MathFin

theorem bond_2nd_immunization_thm
    {ι κ : Type*}
    (sA : Finset ι) (wA TA : ι → ℝ)
    (sL : Finset κ) (wL TL : κ → ℝ)
    (t r : ℝ)
    (h_match_conv : MathFin.bondPortfolioConv sA wA TA t r =
                    MathFin.bondPortfolioConv sL wL TL t r) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv fun r' =>
        MathFin.bondPortfolioValue sA wA TA t r' - MathFin.bondPortfolioValue sL wL TL t r')
      0 r :=
  MathFin.bondPortfolio_immunization_second_order sA wA TA sL wL TL t r h_match_conv

metadata.reference: Second-order Redington immunization (Fabozzi Ch 5; Hull Ch 4.11)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, stated for the surplus A − L itself: the second derivative of each side is its convexity-times-value (hasDerivAt_neg_bondPortfolioDur_r, the r-derivative of −Dur·P), so matching those makes the r-derivative of the dollar-duration gap vanish. That is transported to `deriv` of the surplus by hasDerivAt_deriv_of_eventually (Foundations/DerivOfDeriv.lean), since the dollar-duration gap is ∂(A − L)/∂r at every r (hasDerivAt_bondPortfolioValue_r on each side). Lives in MathFin/FixedIncome/ConvexityImmunization.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Yield Curve Bootstrap: General Solve
theorems.description: From the coupon-bond pricing equation P = ∑ c_i·B_i + (c_n + F)·B_n, the new ZCB price is B_n = (P - ∑ c_i·B_i)/(c_n + F).

    B_last = (P - ∑ i ∈ sprev, c i * B i) / (c_last + F) :=
  MathFin.bootstrap_solve sprev c B P c_last F B_last h hP

theorems.name: Vasicek Terminal Distribution is Gaussian (Wiener Representation)
theorems.description: The Vasicek short-rate SDE dr = κ(θ − r)dt + σ dB has the textbook solution r_T = r₀e^{−κT} + θ(1 − e^{−κT}) + σ ∫₀ᵀ e^{−κ(T−s)} dB_s (cited, not proved here). For κ > 0 and r_T in this Wiener representation, this theorem DERIVES (no longer posits) the terminal law r_T ~ N(vasicekSDEMean, vasicekSDEVariance) = N(r₀e^{−κT}+θ(1−e^{−κT}), σ²(1−e^{−2κT})/(2κ)). The stochastic term is the Wiener integral of the DETERMINISTIC integrand e^{−κ(T−s)}, hence Gaussian (sc-wiener-integral-gaussian) with variance its squared L²-norm ∫₀ᵀ e^{−2κ(T−s)} ds = (1−e^{−2κT})/(2κ) (an FTC computation); the affine map x ↦ mean + σx then sends N(0, ∫kernel²) to N(mean, σ²·∫kernel²) = N(vasicekSDEMean, vasicekSDEVariance) via gaussianReal_const_mul / gaussianReal_const_add. This is the FIRST consumer of the deterministic-integrand Itô tower in the FixedIncome layer — the analytic Wiener/Itô machinery made load-bearing in a pricing module, closing the two-tower gap for the Vasicek short rate (VasicekSDE.lean previously stated this law without derivation).

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.VasicekSDEGaussian

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

theorem vasicek_sde_terminal_gaussian
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ)
    (r₀ θ σ : ℝ) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    HasLaw (fun ω => vasicekSDEMean r₀ θ κ (T : ℝ)
        + σ * (wienerIntegralLp B hB T (vasicekKernelLp κ hκ.le T) ω))
      (gaussianReal (vasicekSDEMean r₀ θ κ (T : ℝ))
        (vasicekSDEVariance σ κ (T : ℝ)).toNNReal) μ :=
  MathFin.vasicekShortRate_hasLaw_gaussian hB r₀ θ σ hκ T

theorems.name: Vasicek Zero-Coupon Bond Price (Affine Term Structure)
theorems.description: The Vasicek zero-coupon bond price P(0,T) = E[exp(-∫₀ᵀ r_s ds)], the expectation taken under the probability measure that carries the Brownian driver (read as the pricing measure; no change of measure is built in this entry). Under Vasicek the integrated short rate ∫₀ᵀ r_s ds = M(T) + σ∫₀ᵀ g dB is again Gaussian (integrated OU kernel g(u) = (1-e^{-κ(T-u)})/κ), so the bond price is a Gaussian Laplace transform and collapses to the classical AFFINE TERM STRUCTURE P(0,T) = A(T)·exp(-B(T)·r₀) with B(T) = (1-e^{-κT})/κ. The exponential-affine dependence on the initial short rate r₀ is the defining property of an affine term-structure model.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.VasicekBondPrice

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

/-- **Vasicek zero-coupon bond price — the affine term structure.**
The risk-neutral present value `P(0,T) = 𝔼[exp(−∫₀ᵀ r_s ds)]` of one unit paid
at `T` under the Vasicek short-rate model separates the initial rate into the
exponential-affine form `P(0,T) = A(T)·exp(−B(T)·r₀)`, `B(T) = (1−e^{−κT})/κ`.
Re-exports `MathFin.vasicekBondPrice_affine`. -/
theorem vasicek_bond_price_affine
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ)
    (r₀ θ σ : ℝ) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-(vasicekIntegratedRate hB r₀ θ σ hκ T ω)) ∂μ
      = vasicekBondA θ σ κ (T : ℝ) * Real.exp (-(vasicekBondB κ (T : ℝ) * r₀)) :=
  MathFin.vasicekBondPrice_affine hB r₀ θ σ hκ T

metadata.reference: Vasicek 1977 short-rate model; the affine zero-coupon bond price P(0,T) = A(T)·exp(-B(T)·r₀)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export from MathFin.FixedIncome.VasicekBondPrice (vasicekBondPrice_affine). The Vasicek zero-coupon bond price P(0,T) = E[exp(-int_0^T r_s ds)] as the Gaussian Laplace transform of the integrated short rate, collapsing to the affine term structure P = A(T)*exp(-B(T)*r0), B(T) = (1-e^{-kappa T})/kappa. The integrated rate int_0^T r_s ds = M(T) + sigma*int_0^T g dB is carried in its Wiener representation (integrated OU kernel g(u) = (1-e^{-kappa(T-u)})/kappa; the deterministic time-order swap is the modelling bridge, cited not proven -- parity with the OU-solution model of mf-vasicek-sde-terminal-gaussian). Its Gaussian law N(M, sigma^2 V) follows from wienerIntegralLp_hasLaw_gaussian + the FTC variance integral int_0^T g^2 = V(T) (vasicekIntegratedKernel_integral_sq, antiderivative u/kappa^2 - 2e^{-kappa(T-u)}/kappa^3 + e^{-2kappa(T-u)}/(2kappa^3)); the bond price factors exp(-M)*E[exp(-sigma*int g dB)] = exp(-M + sigma^2 V/2) via the centred Gaussian MGF integral_exp_mul_gaussianReal_zero at -sigma. Second consumer of the deterministic-integrand Wiener tower in FixedIncome. Axioms-clean: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

theorems.name: CIR Affine Loading B(T) Solves the Riccati Equation
theorems.description: For the Cox–Ingersoll–Ross short rate dr = κ(θ − r)dt + σ√r dW, in the affine form P(0,T) = exp(A(T) − B(T)·r₀) of its bond price, the closed-form rate loading B(T) = 2(e^{γT} − 1)/((γ + κ)(e^{γT} − 1) + 2γ), γ = √(κ² + 2σ²), solves the Riccati equation B'(T) = 1 − κB(T) − ½σ²B(T)² with B(0) = 0, at every real T, whenever κ² + 2σ² > 0. Only this equation is verified: the bond price itself is not derived.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.CIRRiccati

open MathFin

/-- **The CIR rate loading solves the Riccati equation.** With `γ = √(κ² + 2σ²)`, the closed
form `B(T) = 2(e^{γT} − 1) / ((γ + κ)(e^{γT} − 1) + 2γ)` of the CIR affine bond price
`P(0,T) = exp(A(T) − B(T)·r₀)` satisfies `B(0) = 0` and `B'(T) = 1 − κB(T) − ½σ²B(T)²` at every
`T`, whenever `κ² + 2σ² > 0`. Re-exports `MathFin.cirBondB_zero` and
`MathFin.hasDerivAt_cirBondB`. -/
theorem cir_bond_B_solves_riccati {κ σ : ℝ} (h : 0 < κ ^ 2 + 2 * σ ^ 2) :
    cirBondB κ σ 0 = 0 ∧
      ∀ T : ℝ, HasDerivAt (cirBondB κ σ)
        (1 - κ * cirBondB κ σ T - σ ^ 2 / 2 * cirBondB κ σ T ^ 2) T :=
  ⟨cirBondB_zero κ σ, hasDerivAt_cirBondB h⟩

theorems.name: CIR Affine Loading A(T) Solves A' = −κθB
theorems.description: For the Cox–Ingersoll–Ross short rate, in the affine form P(0,T) = exp(A(T) − B(T)·r₀) of its bond price, the closed-form level loading A(T) = (2κθ/σ²)·log(2γe^{(κ+γ)T/2} / ((γ + κ)(e^{γT} − 1) + 2γ)), γ = √(κ² + 2σ²), satisfies A(0) = 0 and A'(T) = −κθB(T) at every real T, whenever σ ≠ 0. Only this equation is verified: the bond price itself is not derived.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.CIRRiccati

open MathFin

/-- **The CIR level loading solves its equation.** In the affine form
`P(0,T) = exp(A(T) − B(T)·r₀)`, the closed form `A(T) = (2κθ/σ²)·log(2γ e^{(κ+γ)T/2} / D(T))`,
with `γ = √(κ² + 2σ²)` and `D(T) = (γ + κ)(e^{γT} − 1) + 2γ`, satisfies `A(0) = 0` and
`A'(T) = −κθ B(T)` at every `T`, whenever `σ ≠ 0`. Re-exports `MathFin.cirBondA_zero` and
`MathFin.hasDerivAt_cirBondA`. -/
theorem cir_bond_A_solves_equation {κ σ : ℝ} (θ : ℝ) (hσ : σ ≠ 0) :
    cirBondA κ θ σ 0 = 0 ∧
      ∀ T : ℝ, HasDerivAt (cirBondA κ θ σ) (-(κ * θ) * cirBondB κ σ T) T :=
  ⟨cirBondA_zero κ θ σ, hasDerivAt_cirBondA κ θ hσ⟩

theorems.name: Forward Price under the T-Forward Measure
theorems.description: The T-forward measure Q^T is the pricing measure with the zero-coupon bond P(·,T) as numéraire. Its defining property is that the forward price is the Q^T-expectation of the spot: E^{Q^T}[S_T] = S_0/P(0,T) = S_0·e^{rT} = F(0,T), the no-arbitrage forward price. Built as a change-of-numéraire instance (bond slots N_T = P(T,T) = 1, N_0 = P(0,T) = e^{-rT}, money-market reference B_T = e^{rT}, B_0 = 1), the natural next numéraire instance after the stock and exchange-option S²-numéraires.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.ForwardMeasure

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin

/-- **Black–Scholes forward price under the T-forward measure.**
With the zero-coupon bond `P(·,T)` as numéraire, the forward price of the spot is
its `Q^T`-expectation: `𝔼^{Q^T}[S_T] = S_0·e^{rT} = S_0/P(0,T) = F(0,T)`, the
no-arbitrage forward price. Re-exports `MathFin.forwardMeasure_bs_expected_terminal`. -/
theorem forward_measure_bs_expected_terminal
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S_0 K r σ T : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ} (h : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K r σ T Z) :
    ∫ ω, bsTerminal S_0 r σ T (Z ω) ∂(forwardMeasure Q r T) = S_0 * Real.exp (r * T) :=
  MathFin.forwardMeasure_bs_expected_terminal h

The T-forward measure Q^T (zero-coupon bond P(.,T) as numeraire) satisfies E^{Q^T}[S_T] = S_0*e^{rT} = S_0/P(0,T) = F(0,T), the no-arbitrage forward price. Built as a numeraireMeasure instance (N_T = P(T,T) = 1, N_0 = P(0,T) = e^{-rT}, reference B_T = e^{rT}, B_0 = 1) on the change-of-numeraire engine (MathFin.changeOfNumeraire, no integrability hypothesis): forwardMeasure_price gives e^{-rT}*E^{Q^T}[X] = E^Q[e^{-rT}X] for any claim, and combined with the discounted-terminal EMM property discounted_terminal_eq_S0 yields the forward price of the BS terminal. HONEST SCOPE: in the constant-rate ZCB the density dQ^T/dQ = 1 so Q^T = Q coincides with the risk-neutral measure (the construction generalizes verbatim to a stochastic short rate where Q^T != Q). Natural next numeraire instance after the stock and S^2-numeraires. Axioms-clean: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

theorems.name: Vanilla Interest-Rate Swap: Zero Value iff Par Swap Rate
theorems.description: Vanilla interest-rate swap: annuity, payer-swap value, par swap rate, and the par identity over the zcb curve.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.InterestRateSwap

open MathFin

/-- Vanilla interest-rate swap par identity on the zcb curve: with a positive daycount and a nonempty payment schedule, the payer swap is worth zero iff the fixed rate is the par swap rate. -/
theorem mf_fixedincome_swap {ι : Type*} (r δ K T0 Tn : ℝ) (T : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    payerSwapValue (zcb r 0 T0) (zcb r 0 Tn) K (annuity δ (fun i ↦ zcb r 0 (T i)) s) = 0 ↔
      K = parSwapRate (zcb r 0 T0) (zcb r 0 Tn) (annuity δ (fun i ↦ zcb r 0 (T i)) s) :=
  MathFin.payerSwapValue_zcb_eq_zero_iff r δ K T0 Tn T s hδ hs

theorems.name: Forward-rate agreement value and fair-rate identity
theorems.description: The simple forward rate implied by two zero-coupon bonds gives the FRA discount-factor value, and the FRA is worth zero exactly at that rate.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.FRA

open MathFin

/-- The ZCB-implied simple forward rate expands the FRA value to the discount-factor difference, and it is the unique fixed rate giving zero value. -/
theorem mf_fixedincome_fra (r δ K T1 T2 : ℝ) (hδ : δ ≠ 0) :
    fraValue δ (zcb r 0 T2) (fraForwardRate (zcb r 0 T1) (zcb r 0 T2) δ) K =
        zcb r 0 T1 - zcb r 0 T2 - δ * zcb r 0 T2 * K
      ∧ (fraValue δ (zcb r 0 T2) (fraForwardRate (zcb r 0 T1) (zcb r 0 T2) δ) K = 0 ↔
        K = fraForwardRate (zcb r 0 T1) (zcb r 0 T2) δ) :=
  ⟨MathFin.fraValue_zcb_eq_discount_difference r δ K T1 T2 hδ,
   MathFin.fraValue_zcb_eq_zero_iff r δ K T1 T2 hδ⟩

/-- Caplet-floorlet parity, the forward-rate analogue of put-call parity. -/
